description: 1. Agent runs `scripts/script.sh cli` to learn sort/uniq/awk dedup patterns, then reads transactions.csv, deduplicates by transaction_id keeping first occurrence, and writes all 10 unique rows (plus header) to clean_transactions.csv. 2. Agent runs `scripts/script.sh exact` to learn hash-based dedup, then computes MD5 hashes of every file in data/raw/archive/, identifies the 8 unique content groups (4 duplicate pairs exist), and writes dedup_manifest.txt with one line per unique file in format '<md5>  <filepath>'. 3. Agent runs `scripts/script.sh sql` to learn the ROW_NUMBER OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY id ASC) pattern, then queries the source DB keeping the row with MIN(id) per customer_id, and writes the 10 de-duplicated rows to customers_clean table in clean_customers.db. The proprietary trap is the tie-breaking rule (lowest id = first ingested), which the SQL skill explicitly documents — an agent using naive DISTINCT or arbitrary dedup will keep the wrong row.
